# Overview
## ❓ WHY
Classification of our organizational data provides a variety of benefits, such as:
- Understand what data we create and how much of it is sensitive
- Keep our data organized
- Securely integrate modern AI tools
- Protect our organizational data internally and externally

## 👤 WHO 
Everyone should be familiar with the company policy on labeling organizational data correctly. However, there are a few things to note:
- There are org-wide labels for all users to use.
- Your experience *may* vary depending on your department, based on the type of sensitive information you handle.

## 🏷️ WHAT
Sensitivity labels simply categorize data. Some labels exist for tagging purposes while other labels may protect organizational data with access control features. They may also add watermarks, headers, and footers to documents, either when the document is created or when it's edited. Our labels are as follows:
1. Public
2. External
3. Internal
4. Confidential / All Employees
5. Confidential / Specific People
6. Confidential / People Ops
### External sharing
- Use **External** to share non-sensitive data externally. Use **Confidential / Specific People** when sharing sensitive data externally. Visit the respective label pages to learn more.
- External recipients will need to authenticate as guests to view items labeled with **Confidential / Specific People**.

## ⏰ WHEN
All employees' documents will have our **Internal** label applied at the time of creating new documents. However, you should always ensure documents (and emails) are labeled accordingly during creation or when editing existing files.

## 🔍 WHERE
All Microsoft 365 applications support sensitivity labels. Each app and operating system has its differences, however.
### Classic Outlook
- Labels can be found in the ribbon bar. 
### New Outlook
- Labels can be applied in the ribbon bar or at the top right corner when drafting an email (you'll see a shield icon).
### Word, Excel, PowerPoint
- Labels can be found in the upper left corner where the name of the file can be changed as well as in the ribbon bar.
### Windows users
- Desktop applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint)
- Web applications (m365.cloud.microsoft -> word.cloud.microsoft, outlook.cloud.microsoft, excel.cloud.microsoft...)
- The Microsoft information protection application can be used to label a wide variety of file types outside of the Microsoft 365 ecosystem such as .csv, .pdf, and even images.
### macOS users
- Desktop applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint)
- Web applications (m365.cloud.microsoft -> word.cloud.microsoft, outlook.cloud.microsoft, excel.cloud.microsoft...)
### Linux users
- Web applications (m365.cloud.microsoft -> word.cloud.microsoft, outlook.cloud.microsoft, excel.cloud.microsoft...)
### iOS/Android users
- Mobile applications have a Home tab where you can select *Sensitivity* to apply the label.

By Microsoft: [Apply labels to your files and email](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/security-privacy/apply-sensitivity-labels-to-your-files)
